problems.problem: The reading does not line up with the key verse the reader sees above it. Griffith prints the three places as ‘in mid-air, in the heaven, and in the waters’, but his ‘mid-air’ translates samudra, which Sāyaṇa takes as the ocean (समुद्रे अब्धौ वडवानलरूपेण), and Sāyaṇa takes Griffith’s ‘the waters’ as mid-air (आपः इति अन्तरिक्षनाम ... वैद्युताग्निरूपेण). The sentence says only that he takes ‘the waters’ as a name for mid-air. A reader therefore matches the lightning to Griffith’s ‘mid-air’ and cannot tell where the fire beneath the ocean sits in the verse. The attribution is right, but the sentence is not clear or exact for its reader.
problems.fix: Say which place is which, in Sāyaṇa’s own terms: ‘In a hymn to Agni as a newborn infant, the verse counts his births; Sāyaṇa, on 1.95.3, reads the three as the fire beneath the ocean, the sun in heaven and the lightning, taking the first place as the sea and ‘the waters’ as mid-air.’ (45 words; passes entry-check in scratch/crit2-d12.json).

problems.problem: Spread. Sāyaṇa is the only commentator on 31 of 32 days (the gate warns that he holds every day), and Yāska appears only as the second name on day 22. Yet the packet shows the Nirukta treating the key verse on 12 days (1.1.1, 1.22.17, 1.32.1, 1.41.9, 1.84.15, 1.115.1, 1.164.46, 1.170.1, 1.181.4, 1.185.1, 2.38.4). On 1.22.17 Yāska has a real comment of his own that differs from Sāyaṇa’s: Nirukta 12.19 gives the three steps as places, on earth, in mid-air and in heaven (Śākapūṇi), or on the mountain of sunrise, the meridian and the mountain of sunset (Aurṇavābha), where Sāyaṇa gives the Trivikrama descent. The refuted revision put the two men side by side, and Sāyaṇa quotes this very passage as his gloss, so it was rightly withdrawn. Yāska alone on this day is still open, and it is the clearest place in the batch where the other roster voice has something distinct to say.
problems.fix: Give day 2 to Yāska alone: ‘Near the close of a hymn to many gods, six verses turn to Visnu and his strides; Yāska, Nirukta 12.19, explains the three steps by two teachers’ views: on earth, mid-air and heaven, or on the mountains of sunrise and sunset and the meridian between.’ Set by to yaska and src to ‘Yāska, Nirukta 12.19, trans. Lakshman Sarup, The Nighantu and the Nirukta (1920 to 1921), archive.org nighantuniruktao00yask’. Take the evidence from Sarup’s 12.19 in the packet (with the Sanskrit that Sāyaṇa quotes: पृथिव्यामन्तरिक्षे दिवीति शाकपूणिः समारोहणे विष्णुपदे गयशिरसीत्यौर्णवाभः). The sentence is 45 words and passes entry-check in scratch/crit2-d2.json. It keeps Sarup’s mountains as places and does not turn them into times of day. Re-verify before it lands.
